A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DINOv2 concept-analysis and Minkowski Representation Hypothesis study. Matching text, equations, Figures 1–28, and appendices A–K support reliable comparison despite local header/figure overlaps in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-recruitment, image-perturbation, positional-decoding, dictionary-geometry, and reconstruction results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including task comparisons, positional-decoding analyses, and archetypal reconstruction experiments in Figures 3, 14, and 17.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same convex-hull-constrained SAE, BatchTopK encoder, 32,000-atom dictionary, and eight active codes per token. The concept-importance procedure is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Figure 2 retains ImageNet-1K classification, ADE20K segmentation, and NYU Depth V2 depth estimation. The ImageNet geometry studies and controlled image-perturbation scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The random and shuffled co-activation baselines, random and Grassmannian dictionary comparators, and AA-versus-SAE reconstruction comparison remain unchanged. Newly cited methods are not added to the evaluated comparisons.

E3.justification: Both retain the same DINOv2-B configuration, 50-epoch SAE training, top-100 and top-500 concept analyses, and ImageNet validation protocol for MRH experiments. No experimental settings or evaluation metrics are revised.

E4.justification: The Elsewhere masking analysis, five depth-cue perturbations, task-subspace controls, and positional-removal analyses remain unchanged, including the supporting results in appendices C–I.

E5.justification: Uncertainty displays, including the shaded bands in Figure 17, and significance statements are retained. No seed information, repeated-run counts, uncertainty-estimation methods, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Reported values and findings match, including reconstruction R² > 88% in Section 2, correlation r = 0.28 and R² = 0.08 in Figure 11, and the AA/SAE reconstruction curves in Figure 17. Appendix results are also retained.

T1.justification: The LRH and MRH definitions, attention-to-polytope derivations, affine-preservation results, and non-identifiability propositions and proofs are unchanged, including Appendix J.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: the 32,000-concept dictionary, task-specific concept families, structured representation geometry, and MRH proposal.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations and limitations are retained. Section 7.2 and Appendix J.6 still describe MRH as a preliminary working hypothesis, with observational, model-specific evidence and non-identifiable decompositions.

D1.justification: Both provide the same DinoVision link and implementation information, including 8,000 RISE forward passes, the six-hour A100 Grassmannian computation, and 1,024-step feature accentuation.

R1.justification: v2 adds Klindt et al. (2025) to the SAE discussion and Shafran et al. (2026), described as MFAs, and Park et al. (2026) to the geometric precedents in Section 7.1. These modestly extend the bibliography and background without redefining the contribution.

P1.justification: v2 adopts conference-style title and section headings and changes the publication-status text. Apart from small wording and citation-bearing sentence edits, the narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: All 28 figures are retained, with altered rendering resolution, spacing, link colors, and placement; Figure 6 moves from page 9 to page 8. The new running header overlaps figure titles and plot regions, notably in Figures 10 and 14.

improvement.justification: The added references modestly update the background, and some graphics are sharper. However, v2 introduces running-header overlaps with figure titles and plots, particularly Figures 10 and 14, reducing legibility. The scientific content is preserved, but these presentation defects produce a limited overall quality decline.
